chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would use perfume when he fasted, and he would say, 'Perfume is the gift of the fasting person.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use perfume while fasting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Sunnah of maintaining physical elegance during voluntary fasting, distinguishing it from the asceticism often associated with obligatory fasts. The description of perfume as the 'gift of the fasting person' reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with worldly refinement, affirming that scent enhances the dignity of the worshipper without invalidating the fast.
